question: A 3-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his parents for a well-child examination. The boy was born at term via vaginal delivery and has been healthy except for impaired vision due to severe short-sightedness. He is at the 97th percentile for height and 25th percentile for weight. Oral examination shows a high-arched palate. He has abnormally long, slender fingers and toes, and his finger joints are hyperflexible. The patient is asked to place his thumbs in the palms of the same hand and then clench to form a fist. The thumbs are noted to protrude beyond the ulnar border of the hand. Slit lamp examination shows lens subluxation in the superotemporal direction bilaterally. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Mutation in fibrillin-1 gene -> Marfan syndrome features (high-arched palate, long fingers, hyperflexible joints) -> Lens subluxation -> 95%
CHAIN: Defective collagen cross-linking -> Connective tissue abnormalities (high-arched palate, long fingers, hyperflexible joints) -> Lens subluxation -> 90%
enhanced_information: The most likely underlying cause of this patient's condition is a mutation in the fibrillin-1 gene, leading to Marfan syndrome. This is supported by the presence of characteristic features such as high-arched palate, long fingers, hyperflexible joints, and lens subluxation, which are commonly seen in Marfan syndrome.
analysis: The patient's presentation with features such as high-arched palate, long fingers, hyperflexible joints, and lens subluxation is highly suggestive of Marfan syndrome. Marfan syndrome is primarily caused by a mutation in the fibrillin-1 gene, leading to structural abnormalities in connective tissue. This aligns with the enhanced information provided.
